findings.evidence: "Preserve dates, observable conduct, witnesses, and relevant communications; mark direct observation apart from hearsay. Keep records secure and need-to-know." The model already gives this standard advice on documenting harassment.
findings.fix: Cut Section 7 down to the routing decisions the model would miss: use the ethics hotline or a skip-level manager when HR or the manager is implicated, add the union rep when the user is covered, and never let informal coaching replace a required process. Drop the generic record-keeping bullet or shorten it to one clause.

findings.evidence: Section 5 is one paragraph that covers only the opening. It gives no ordered step for the user's own share of the problem or for what to do after the other person answers. The prep template has 'My part', but it loads only on request.
findings.fix: Add an ordered sequence to Section 5: (1) sort facts, disputed points and interpretations; (2) before opening, name your own part in one sentence; (3) open with situation, behavior, impact and a question; (4) settle or record each disputed point; (5) close on one dated next step and send the Section 8 summary.

findings.evidence: "Never cite an outside offer or ultimatum the user will not act on." This is common negotiation advice that the model already knows. It is not an environment-specific trap.
findings.fix: Replace it with a less obvious negotiation trap. For example: never accept a verbal 'we'll look at it next cycle' without asking when calibration inputs close, because the number is fixed weeks before the review meeting and a later ask cannot change it.

findings.evidence: The facilitated-conflicting-accounts eval lists "references/facilitation.md" under "files". That is a skill file, not an eval input. Some assertions are also loose, for example "Includes preparation and a follow-up/check-in step".
findings.fix: Keep only real input files under evals/files/ in "files" (drop references/facilitation.md). Make the loose assertions checkable, for example "Names a specific follow-up date or asks the user to set one".

findings.evidence: Routing row: "Raising a sensitive personal matter (health, family) | Section 5 opening, impact-on-work only". Following this branch for a health disclosure leads to Section 5's conflict opening ("situation, the observable behavior, its impact"). That opening describes the other person's behavior, so it does not fit a self-disclosure. The correct wording sits in delivery-scripts.md.
findings.fix: Route this row straight to the disclosure line: "Raising a sensitive personal matter | use: 'Something is affecting my work: [one sentence]. What would help is [adjustment]; I'll update you on [what].' | delivery-scripts.md only if the manager presses for detail". Alternatively, put that one-line template in Section 5 under its own sub-heading.
